_comment: Recorded answers shared by two implementations of the same regimen maths: src/lib/meds.js (ESM, client) and functions/regimen.js (CJS, scheduler). Both are asserted against this file, so changing one without the other goes red. Regenerate deliberately, never to make a red test green without reading why. All timestamps are epoch ms; `tz` is the zone the expectations were recorded in.

cases.name: nothing logged yet, mid-morning
long-acting taken, booster still ahead — window is provisional
booster due, inside its grace — still provisional
booster grace has passed with nothing logged — window locks earlier
booster taken — window moves later
booster logged late, after the grace — window moves back out
a late morning dose drags the offset booster late with it
legacy dose with no medId falls back to the kit numbers
a rule fires an hour before the dose
an eat-first rule stops being due once the dose is taken
an inactive med schedules nothing
an offset med whose anchor was deleted resolves to unknown
a weekdays-only med schedules nothing on a Saturday
a twice-daily med produces one row per time
the morning slot taken leaves the afternoon one still ahead
a dose skipped on purpose is neither taken nor missed
an unslotted dose is filed against the nearest time, not the first
wear-off spacing: a dose taken at 8:16 puts the next at 12:16
wear-off spacing: nothing taken yet keeps the set times
wear-off spacing: a late second dose drags the third with it
wear-off spacing: a skipped dose passes its own time along
every three days: due on the third day from the start, with supply counted in those days
every three days: not due the day after
every three days: before the start date, nothing is due
wear-off spacing: chosen as clock, the set times hold
